title: The 68 NANOGrav 15-year pulsars: spin frequencies and dispersion measures

object.name: Sixty-eight millisecond pulsars
object.frame: timing models in barycentric dynamical time (par UNITS TDB); spin frequency in Hz and dispersion measure in pc/cm3 by the par-file convention of tempo2 and PINT, which the archive does not restate

facility.observatory: Arecibo, the Green Bank Telescope and the Very Large Array (NANOGrav)
facility.pipeline: NANOGrav 15-year data set, release v2.1.0 (Zenodo 10.5281/zenodo.16051178): narrowband and wideband timing models, narrowband/par and wideband/par

license.statement: The Zenodo record 10.5281/zenodo.16051178 (version 2.1.0, published 2025-07-17, creator The NANOGrav Collaboration, access open) states the licence CC BY 4.0 in its licence field (the record's JSON, retrieved 2026-11-05). None of the release's README files states a licence, a citation request or a condition (README and narrowband/README.narrowband were read in full, and every README of the release, including wideband, residuals, clock and the correlations', was searched for licence, copyright, citation, acknowledgement, redistribution, permission and condition terms, 2026-11-05). The README names Agazie et al. 2023 and the record's DOI as the data set's description and home. Attribute: The NANOGrav Collaboration, the NANOGrav 15-year Data Set, v2.1.0, doi:10.5281/zenodo.16051178; Agazie et al. 2023, ApJL 951, L9. The table was extracted and reformatted from the timing models, and the values are summarised as the manifest states.

columns.name: spin frequency
columns.description: the narrowband timing model's F0, in Hz by the par-file convention (the files state no unit), stored to 1e-6 Hz

columns.name: dispersion measure
columns.description: the narrowband model's DM line plus the mean of its DMX epoch offsets, in pc/cm3 by the par-file convention (the files state no unit)

columns.name: dispersion measure, wideband model
columns.description: the same quantity from the wideband timing model of the same pulsar: the only measure of how well two fits of one data set agree, since the files carry no DM uncertainty

columns.name: spread of the DM over epochs
columns.description: the sample standard deviation of DM + DMX over the narrowband model's epochs: the pulsar's DM varies with time and this is by how much

columns.name: DMX epochs
columns.description: the number of DMX epochs of the narrowband model

reductions: 68 rows, one per pulsar of the data set, in the order of the pulsar names (code-unit order: B names, then J). The 8 timing models fitted to one telescope's data alone (B1937+21ao, B1937+21gbt, J1600-3053gbt, J1643-1224gbt, J1713+0747ao, J1713+0747gbt, J1903+0327ao, J1909-3744gbt) are second models of pulsars already in the table and are not rows.

The spin frequency is the F0 of the narrowband timing model (every file fits it), stored to 1e-6 Hz. Its uncertainty, the epoch, every other timing parameter, the times of arrival, the templates and the residuals are not kept.

The DM line of a file is a fixed baseline (no file fits it; 6 give it an uncertainty and a zero fit flag) and the fitted per-epoch offsets (DMX_nnnn) carry the variation, so a pulsar's DM is the baseline plus the mean of the offsets (the column dm), with the sample standard deviation of baseline plus offset over the epochs (dmx_std) and the number of epochs (dmx_n). The mean is unweighted and not time-weighted. The same sum from the wideband models is dm_wb. These are not the data-set paper's tabulated DMs, which were not read.

The files carry no DM uncertainty for 62 of the 68 pulsars and a frozen one for the other 6, so the column is not shipped; the difference between dm and dm_wb is the only scatter the pack offers (median 0.00309 pc/cm3; 3 pulsars differ by more than 0.5: J0610-2100 0.626, J1022+1001 0.837, J1024-0719 1.97).

No unit is written in the files. Hz and pc/cm3 are the par-file convention of the two packages the README names (tempo2 and PINT). The one check the data allow: every spin frequency lies between 29.0 and 641.9 Hz, periods of 1.56 to 34.4 ms, consistent with the data set being of millisecond pulsars.

steps: Inflate the archive as a stream and keep only narrowband/par/*.nb.par and wideband/par/*.wb.par (checking every tar header checksum).
Read PSR, F0 (refusing a file whose F0 is not fitted), DM, DM1, DMEPOCH, PEPOCH, DMDATA, UNITS and every DMX_nnnn offset; the first occurrence of a name wins.
Leave out the single-telescope models (a name that is another pulsar plus ao or gbt) and require 68 pulsars named alike in both sets.
dm = DM + mean(DMX_i) and dm_wb the same from the wideband file; dmx_std = sample standard deviation of DM + DMX_i; dmx_n = the number of epochs.
Store the five columns as table-columns/1.

record.membersDigestOf: the sorted lines 'path-below-the-release-directory TAB sha256' of every member read, joined by newlines

assumptions: The units are the par-file convention (spin frequency in Hz, dispersion measure in pc cm^-3); the archive's files do not state them.
The narrowband models are the data set's primary timing models (its README); the wideband models are a second fit of the same pulsars and are used only for dm_wb.

A pulsar's dispersion measure is not constant: the pack states a mean over the epochs and its spread, and a distance from it (the crude electron-density estimate used in teaching) inherits that spread and the model of the Galaxy's electron density, which is not in this pack.
Every pulsar is a millisecond pulsar timed for years with a model that includes red noise; the periods are those of that model, not a single epoch's measurement.

validation.check: the 68 rows have spin periods between 1 and 100 ms (a bound chosen here, not a published definition), positive dispersion measures, at least two DMX epochs each, and the narrowband and wideband dispersion measures of at least 60 pulsars agree within 0.1 pc/cm3 (a bound set after reading the files, descriptive and not a validation against a published value)

against.ref: the archive's own wideband timing models of the same pulsars, an independent fit of the same data set
